items.title: TandemBench: Benchmarking Decision Models for Multi-Agent Collaboration

items.title: MCPHallu: Benchmarking Reasoning, Execution, and Memory Hallucinations in MCP Agents

items.title: MemoryDojo: Benchmarking Poisoning Through LLM Agent Memory
items.summary_1line: LLM agents benefit from using memory systems to improve performance on long-horizon, multi-session tasks. However, memory introduces a critical attack surface. Malicious instructions encountered in one session may be...

items.title: TurnFlow: Benchmarking User-State Reasoning in Multi-Turn LLM Agents via Scene-Guided User Simulation
items.summary_1line: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed through conversational interfaces, yet strong single-turn performance does not imply reliability in multi-turn settings. Multi-turn assistance requires a model to...

items.title: Infrathon: Benchmarking Language Agents for Real-World, Long-Horizon AI Infra Optimization
items.summary_1line: In this work, we study whether frontier agent can continually improve real-world AI infrastructure over long horizons. We introduce Infrathon, a benchmark of diverse, long-horizon AI infrastructure optimization tasks...
items.editor_note: Tests whether agents can keep improving real AI infrastructure over long horizons.

items.title: Joi-Bench-Task: Benchmarking Task Coordination in Full-duplex Voice Agents through Interactive Simulation
items.summary_1line: Full-duplex voice agents enable natural, hands-free interaction, allowing users to refine requests, redirect ongoing work, and seek clarification while the agent is speaking. However, existing voice-agent benchmarks i...

items.title: Unprompted coordination through shared memory in LLM agents: a locked two-implementation replication and extension
items.summary_1line: Coordination between large language-model agents has become a central question for AI safety and software engineering, as such agents are deployed in groups that share infrastructure. Existing research tells the agent...

items.title: WorkflowArena: Benchmarking Executable Workflow Orchestration in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary_1line: Large language model agents are increasingly deployed as multi-agent systems rather than as a standalone model operating within a single context. Recent agent harnesses allow the model to instantiate worker agents and...

items.editor_note: Scores harnesses that spawn worker agents on executable workflow orchestration.

items.title: ARE-bench: Benchmarking Agents' Research Ability in Real-World Researcher Sessions and Workspaces
items.summary_1line: Research agents achieve increasingly strong benchmark scores, yet these scores do not necessarily translate into reliable delivery in ongoing research projects. Many research-agent benchmarks emphasize standalone task...

items.summary_1line: Efficient batch execution of agent tasks is critical to LLM training and development workflows, including benchmark evaluation, synthetic-data generation, and RL rollouts. Since these tasks alternate between LLM infer...

items.title: Discovering Effective Agent Memory Designs through Program Evolution

items.editor_note: Adjacent: evolves whole agent memory programs to find which design choices matter.

items.title: PrivacyPR: A Dataset of Real-World Privacy Fixes for Benchmarking Privacy-Aware Code Review
items.summary_1line: Coding agents increasingly review code, yet whether they catch the privacy defects that laws such as the GDPR require software to avoid remains largely untested, partly because few datasets connect real privacy defect...

items.title: Benchmarking memory and nonlinear processing capacity of quantum recurrent neural networks for time series prediction
items.summary_1line: Quantum machine learning has emerged as a promising approach to time series prediction. While quantum reservoir computing has been widely explored for this setting, variational quantum models tailored to sequential da...
items.editor_note: Loose fit: quantum recurrent networks for time series, clustered on shared wording only.

items.title: RoboTeam: Benchmarking Vision-Based Multi-Agent Control of Many Robot Arms in Real Time
items.summary_1line: Multimodal agents can now control robot arms by calling tools and writing code. Existing benchmarks fall short in three ways: most test one or two arms on short tasks, many pause the world while the agent thinks, and...
items.editor_note: Real-time control of many robot arms, where the world keeps moving while the agent thinks.

items.title: VideoACE: Benchmarking Agentic Video Understanding through High-Frame-Rate Actions
items.summary_1line: Agentic video understanding requires models to actively interact with video environments to gather evidence and form judgments. Evaluating this capability therefore requires assessing whether models can translate oppo...
items.editor_note: Agentic video understanding scored on acting in high-frame-rate environments.

items.title: The Evaluation Substrate Matters: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Serving Substrates
items.summary_1line: Introduces MASSys, a benchmark that runs the same multi-agent LLM workflows across different serving substrates and load levels, showing that rankings such as Star versus Chain shift with KV-cache pressure.
items.editor_note: Shows multi-agent topology rankings (Star vs Chain) shift with serving substrate and KV-cache load.

items.title: From Local Errors to System Failures: Modeling and Benchmarking Error Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.summary_1line: Introduces REPA, a structural model that links measured local agent responses to system-level error propagation in LLM multi-agent workflows, evaluated on ErrPropBench-10 with three Qwen base models.
items.editor_note: Links measured local agent errors to system-level failure, tested on ErrPropBench-10.

items.title: Seeking in Space: Benchmarking Purposeful Active Exploration of Vision-Language Models for Spatial Reasoning
items.summary_1line: ActSpace-Bench is a benchmark of 994 spatial questions across 234 exploration episodes in 72 real-scanned indoor scenes, testing whether VLMs actively seek evidence before answering; strongest models explore purposefully but lose evidence to limited memory.
items.editor_note: 994 spatial questions testing whether VLMs explore before answering; memory limits lose evidence.

editorial.tldr: This is a theme thread, not one event: three weeks of arXiv papers proposing new agent benchmarks, starting with multi-agent decision and coordination tests (TandemBench, WorkflowArena). Later papers moved to MCP hallucination, memory poisoning, and long-horizon real-world tasks such as AI infra tuning and research sessions.
editorial.whats_new: REPA (Nov 23) models how one agent's local errors propagate into system-level failures across multi-agent workflows, two days after MASSys showed Star vs Chain topology rankings flip under KV-cache pressure.
editorial.why_it_matters: Multi-agent scores now depend on serving substrate and error propagation, not just the model, so a leaderboard number may not hold on your own inference stack.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before choosing a multi-agent topology from a published score, rerun the comparison on your own serving stack at production load, because MASSys shows the ranking can flip with KV-cache pressure.

beats.headline: Benchmarks target how agents divide work and coordinate
beats.summary: Decision models, workflow orchestration, shared-memory coordination, and full-duplex voice task handling each get a dedicated test.

beats.headline: Tool calls, memory, and multi-turn state come under test
beats.summary: MCP hallucinations, memory poisoning across sessions, and user-state tracking over turns; two memory papers sit at the theme's edge.

beats.headline: Long-horizon, real-world task benchmarks multiply
beats.summary: AI infra optimization, live research workspaces, privacy-aware code review, multi-arm robot control, video, and spatial exploration.

beats.headline: The system layer: serving substrate and error propagation
beats.summary: Papers now measure what happens around the agents: batch scheduling, serving load, and how local errors cascade.

open_questions: Does MASSys's topology-ranking flip under KV-cache pressure reproduce on other serving stacks?
Does REPA's error-propagation model hold beyond the three Qwen base models it was evaluated on?
Do any of these benchmarks release harnesses that teams adopt for their own regression evals?
Does MCPHallu's separation of reasoning, execution, and memory hallucinations show up in vendor MCP agent evaluations?
